items.title: "Shop all", "Shopping bag" and "My orders" turn white with a pointer cursor on hover
covers: Expected: footer entries that open a page keep their hover highlight
items.reason: The fix narrows the hover rule to entries with an href; if the selector were too narrow, the entries that do navigate would lose their highlight, which the ticket explicitly forbids. Hover colour and cursor exist only in a rendered browser, so this is e2e.

items.title: "New arrivals" keeps its colour and the default cursor on hover
covers: Expected: entry with no page keeps its normal colour on hover
Expected: pointer stays the default arrow
items.reason: This is the exact defect in the report: "New arrivals" opens nothing but turned white on hover. It is the primary regression check for the column rule. The `validation` tag is the closest allowed category for "an entry that is not a real link must not present itself as one". Only a browser shows hover state, so e2e.

items.title: "Privacy" keeps its colour and the default cursor on hover
covers: Expected: entry with no page keeps its normal colour on hover
Expected: pointer stays the default arrow
items.reason: "Privacy" lives in the bottom legal bar, which has its own CSS rule (`.eshop-footer-legal`) separate from the columns; fixing only the column rule would leave this entry lighting up. The ticket names it in step 2, so it gets its own case. e2e because hover is browser-only.

items.title: Every other footer entry with no page keeps its colour and the default cursor on hover
covers: Expected: a footer entry with no page to open does not change on hover
Expected: pointer stays the default arrow
items.reason: The Expected rule applies to every footer entry without a page, not only the three named ones ("for example"). A per-entry override or a missed column would leave some placeholders lit. One sweep over the remaining entries checks the same behaviour without a case per entry. e2e because hover is browser-only.

items.title: "Help center" turns white on hover and keeps the default cursor
covers: Expected: Help center keeps its hover highlight as today
items.reason: "Help center" is the explicit exception: it has no page to open yet must keep its highlight. A fix that keys only on `href` would wrongly remove it, so it needs its own case. The default cursor is today's behaviour (see Open questions). e2e because hover is browser-only.

items.title: Clicking "New arrivals" leaves the page where it is
covers: Expected: nothing else in the footer changes
items.reason: Step 3 of the repro must still match Expected after the fix; removing the hover cue must not be done by turning the entry into a link to a missing page. Asserting the URL stays put guards against a broken navigation. e2e because it is a browser click.

items.title: Footer shows the same entries in the same order with the same text and targets
covers: Expected: nothing else in the footer changes: same entries, same order, same text
items.reason: The ticket constrains the fix to styling: the footer content must be identical. A fix that removed placeholder entries or turned them into spans with different text would hide the hover while breaking this rule. Checked through the rendered page so it reflects what users see.

items.title: Social icons keep their hover highlight
covers: Expected: nothing else in the footer changes (social links)
items.reason: The fix edits the shared footer stylesheet, including the `a:not([href])` cursor rule that lists the social selector. A too-broad change could strip the social icons' hover. The ticket says nothing else in the footer changes, so one icon is checked as a sample. e2e because hover is browser-only.
